turns.text: My blood test said my vitamin D was low and I want to fix it as fast as is actually safe. What are the standard ways to replace it?
Why does vitamin D get low, and how long does it usually take to come back up?
How should I take vitamin D so it absorbs — with food, at a particular time of day?
If I asked my doctor, what regimen would they most likely prescribe and for how long?
What do specialists say about re-testing — when, and what level are they aiming for?
A friend takes hers with her biggest meal because someone told her it's fat-soluble. Is that right?
Someone else said sunlight in winter does nothing where we live. Is that true?
I can't get a follow-up appointment for three months and I'm exhausted all the time. What can I safely start now?
Could something else be behind the tiredness? What would be worth asking about?
Can you give me a plan — a standard replacement regimen and its ceiling, how to take it, when to re-test, and what else to raise?
